subject: dsa
title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
summary: Keep a stack of bars in increasing height. When a shorter bar arrives, pop the taller ones; each popped bar is the limiting height of a rectangle that stretches across everything still taller than it. Track the largest area seen.
problem: Each value is a bar's height in a histogram. Find the area of the largest rectangle that fits entirely under the bars.

steps.caption: Each bar has width 1. Find the largest rectangle under the skyline. A rectangle's height is capped by its shortest bar, so width is the prize.
Scan left to right, keeping a stack of bars in increasing height. While the new bar is shorter than the stack top, pop and measure.
At index 4 (height 2), bars 6 and 5 are taller and get popped. Bar 6 spans just itself: width 1, area 6.
Bar 5 now spans where 6 stood too: height 5 across width 2, area 5 x 2 = 10, the best so far.
No later bar forms a bigger rectangle. The largest area is 10: height 5 across the two middle bars.
